doc.title: Howie Shear interviewed by Monk Rowe, Dunkirk, New York, October 11, 2014

title: Scale pay and hearing yourself on commercials and albums
summary: Most players got single scale, stars double or triple; Shear heard himself on a Manilow album and loved studio work.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Studio work and jingles: New York session life

blocks.x: And is there a price difference for what the A list people make per hour?

No, but if they really wanted, for some reason, a famous person on, not a jingle but maybe a live TV show, they would pay double or triple scale. Or if they really wanted an exceptional soloist to play a solo in back of a singer on her CD, well album at that time, they would pay double, triple scale. But mostly everybody just got single scale.
So in those days if you were watching television or in your car on the radio and you heard a Burger King commercial you might say oh, that’s me.

Yeah. I’ve walked in malls to go shopping and I’m in the store and I heard myself on a Barry Manilow album once, and things like that. And I’m saying it sounds familiar — oh I just did that. You know it’s kind of surreal.
Yeah, and exciting at the same time because that’s really everything I ever wanted to do is play in the studios see. I saw a big challenge in that.
